title: Bonds and the end of the global savings glut
gist: Three independent fair-value approaches for 10-year Treasurys indicate bond prices have already discounted most of the decline in global excess savings, with the real yield component driving the recent uptrend. Because the post-GFC savings glut has crested and no obvious catalyst exists to reverse the higher yield range, the recommended posture is mean-reversion duration trading rather than directional bets, using a September Fed hike and any resulting yield back-up as an entry point to add duration.

themes.theme: Fair value says the glut is already priced

insights.claim: Three separate approaches to fair value for 10-year Treasurys all conclude that the end of the global savings glut is already reflected in bond prices.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Removes the 'yields must rise further as savings dry up' bull-steepener trade; the structural repricing is behind, not ahead, of the market.
insights.quote: Is the “end of the global savings glut” story reflected in bond prices? Three different approaches to fair value for 10-year Treasurys suggest the answer is yes.

themes.theme: The three pillars of post-GFC excess savings

insights.claim: Persistent excess global savings since the Global Financial Crisis rested on exactly three forces: fiscal austerity, U.S. deleveraging, and Chinese exports.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Gives a three-variable checklist for monitoring whether the savings glut can rebuild and drag yields back down.
insights.quote: Three forces have produced persistent excess global savings since the GFC: fiscal austerity, U.S. deleveraging and Chinese exports.

insights.claim: Two of the three pillars of the post-GFC savings glut — fiscal austerity and U.S. household deleveraging — have already unwound.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Explains the structural bid for higher real yields and why fiscal expansion, not cyclical inflation, is the dominant bond risk.
insights.quote: The first two have unwound, while the third may be constrained by protectionism.

insights.claim: Protectionism is the mechanism that could constrain Chinese exports, the last remaining pillar of the global savings glut.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Trade policy escalation becomes a bond-market variable: more protectionism means less recycled Chinese surplus and structurally higher global yields.

insights.claim: The multi-decade bull market in bonds was driven by the global savings glut, and that glut has now crested rather than merely paused.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: The 40-year duration tailwind is over; total-return expectations for fixed income should be reset to carry plus range trading.

themes.theme: Trade the range, not the direction

insights.claim: The absence of a savings shortage combined with the absence of any obvious catalyst to reverse the shift means 10-year yields should settle into a higher range rather than trend in either direction.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Favors range-bound vol selling and mean-reversion over structural short- or long-duration convictions.
insights.quote: This is not to say we are in a savings shortage, but that there are no obvious catalysts to reverse the shift to a higher range.
insights.locator: This is not to say we are in a savings shortage

insights.claim: The prescribed bond posture is an explicit mean-reversion duration strategy instead of directional bets on yields.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Concrete positioning instruction: fade extremes in the 10-year rather than running a persistent duration tilt.
insights.quote: Investors should therefore adopt a mean-reversion duration strategy rather than place directional bets.

themes.theme: September Fed hike as a duration entry point

insights.claim: Markets are discounting close to a 50% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in September 2026.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: A near-coin-flip pricing means a hike is only half-discounted, so the yield reaction to a hike could be sizeable in either direction.
insights.quote: Markets are currently discounting close to a 50% chance of a Fed hike in September.
insights.locator: Markets are currently discounting close to a 50%

insights.claim: A September Fed hike that pushes yields higher should be treated as an opportunity to add duration rather than as confirmation of a bear market in bonds.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Pre-commits a buy trigger: set duration-add levels ahead of the September FOMC instead of reacting after the fact.
insights.quote: If that occurs and yields back up, we would treat it as an opportunity to add duration.
